thread:
morgan: CI turned red on main @ 4871234567 — intermittent failure in unit tests for serving runtime. Failing test: test_retry_window_alignment. Appears ~1/30 runs. CI log attached by bot below.
ci-bot: [ci] build #8421 failed on linux-x86-64 (runner-7). Failed tests: runtime::test_retry_window_alignment. Artifacts: /artifacts/8421/log.txt
samir: thanks—can you paste the failing stack or last few lines from the log?
morgan: sure, here's tail:
```
FAILED tests/runtime/test_retry_window_alignment.rs:123
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at 'assertion failed: expected 0 pending retries, got 1', src/retry/mod.rs:58:10
---
Time: 00:00:12.457 | event: retry_scheduled id=0x7ff1 seq=42
Time: 00:00:12.459 | event: backoff_wakeup id=0x7ff1 seq=42
Time: 00:00:12.460 | event: retry_executed id=0x7ff1 seq=42 result=Ok
Time: 00:00:12.460 | event: session_end id=0x7ff1
```
katie: looks like a race between backoff wakeup and session cleanup. Is this only on CI or reproducible locally?
morgan: couldn't repro locally with quick runs. Tried `cargo test --test runtime -- --nocapture -p runtime_test test_retry_window_alignment` x10, passed. CI flags include `--jobs 8` and `RUST_TEST_THREADS=8`.
diego: maybe scheduler timing with multiproc parallelism. Can you try a stress loop with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` and then `RUST_TEST_THREADS=8` to compare? also try forcing a deterministic seed: `TEST_SEED=314159 cargo test ...`
samir: also try toggling `--test-threads` and run >=100 iterations, e.g. `for i in {1..200}; do TEST_SEED=$RANDOM cargo test ... || { echo "failed on seed $TEST_SEED"; break; } done` — if we can capture a seed we can bisect.
morgan: starting a 200-run loop on runner VM now (I'll paste seed if it fails). Also kicked a CI rerun for build 8421 (ci-bot: rerun requested).
ci-bot: [ci] re-run queued for build #8421 (retries left: 2)
katie: if this repros, add `env_logger` dump around retry scheduling to dump timestamps and monotonic ticks. Might help distinguish real clock vs. fake monotonic.
diego: hypothesis: flaky when `tokio::time::sleep` uses system clock adjustments vs monotonic. We had a similar flake months ago. Could also be affected by `--jobs` task switching.
samir: can we try reproduce with `RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-generate"`? maybe heavy instrumentation changes timing. but simpler: add `--exact` to isolate test, run in a tiny harness that loops.
morgan: update: ran 200 loops locally with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=8` — pass. Ran 200 loops with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` — pass. Kicked off forced runs on a heavier host with 16 vCPUs. If it hits I'll post seed.
ci-bot: [ci] build #8421 re-run failed again — runtime::test_retry_window_alignment failed on runner-12. Artifacts uploaded.
morgan: the failing CI run included extra log: shows a wakeup at 12.459 but retry_executed logged after session_end — so callback executed after teardown.
katie: ok that's a clear ordering violation between the session lifetime and scheduled retry tasks. Short-term patch: make the test await a flush of scheduled tasks on session drop or add `session.shutdown().await` before assert. Longer-term: change retry scheduler to cancel pending tasks on session drop.
diego: I can put together a small bisect script to determine the commit that introduced non-cancellation. But first let's try to capture a failing seed locally and add a repro test harness with `tokio::time::pause()` + manual advance to make test deterministic.
samir: +1 on harness with paused time, that's more robust than relying on timing. If we add that pattern to the failing test we can unflake quickly.
morgan: plan: (1) add local harness using paused tokio time in PR, (2) open an issue for scheduler cancellation behavior, (3) if CI reproduces with seed I'll post it here and attach minimal bisect script. I'll update in ~1h.
katie: thanks — ping me on the PR for quick review. :thumbsup:
diego: I'll draft the bisect tool in parallel in case we need it.
morgan: update 30m: found failing seed on CI rerun: SEED=83291. Reproduced locally with seed and `--test-threads=8`. Posting gist of failing run and minimal repro in a follow-up PR.
samir: great — with seed we can bisect. if you need help running bisect let me know.
morgan: thanks all, moving to PR now.
